afterburner.option.shaderpacks.tooltip: Choose a shader pack and change its settings.
afterburner.shaders.title: Shader Packs
afterburner.shaders.profile.tooltip: Sets many of the pack's options at once. Left click for the next profile, right click for the one before.
afterburner.shaders.reset.tooltip: Puts all of this pack's settings back to the pack's defaults.
afterburner.option.shadowUpdates.tooltip:
How often a shader pack's shadows are drawn again. Drawing them is much of what a pack costs.

Smart: only when something in them changed (a block, the sun moving on, you moving a block or two), but packs whose leaves and grass wave in their shadows get those (not the rest) drawn again every frame, so they wave smoothly.
When Needed: only when something changed; waving shadows stand still. The fastest.
Every Frame: every frame, as other shader loaders do.
afterburner.option.shaderpack.tooltip:
Click to choose from the packs in .minecraft/shaderpacks (zips, or folders with a shaders folder in them).

OpenGL only for now. Shadows are cast by blocks only (not mobs or water) and need Batched chunk drawing on.
afterburner.option.upscale.tooltip:
Draws the world smaller, then scales it up to the screen with AMD FSR 1 and sharpens it. Lower is faster but softer; the percent is how much of the screen's width is drawn.

Works with and without a shader pack; with one, all of the pack's passes are drawn smaller too. Menus and the hotbar stay sharp.

It helps when the graphics card holds the game back (high resolution, shader packs), and does little when the CPU does (many chunks or mobs). On integrated graphics without a shader pack, it can cost more than it saves.
afterburner.option.farTerrainDistance.to:
How far plain colored far-away terrain reaches, 16 to 1024 chunks (far left: off). It's built from land you've seen, so new worlds fill in as you travel. Takes effect when you let go of the slider. Not drawn while a shader pack is on.

Further costs more video memory and GPU time.
afterburner.option.unseenLand.tooltip:
Fills the far terrain where you've never been with land worked out from the world's seed: the ground's shape, biomes, grass, sand, snow and the sea. No trees, caves or buildings; when you get there, the real land replaces it. Single player, Overworld only. Made on one background thread, nearest first.

Off: only land you've seen is drawn (land already made stays until you see the real thing).
